goal: Verify, by live measurement, every behavioral claim the guide and API doc make about sketch.splitCurve — the new structured-result splitter (Array<{sourceId, splittedCurves:[{id, interval}]}>) that replaces the deprecated flat-array splitCurves. Establish with numeric proof (getPositions / getPoints coordinates, never snapshots alone) that: (1) values are normalized [0,1] fractions mapping linearly along the curve; (2) N values produce N+1 segments on OPEN curves; (3) intervals are true contiguous [0,1] fractions that cover the whole source and cross-check against measured world coordinates; (4) the original curve id is replaced/invalidated after the split; (5) splitCurve is standalone (no preTrim staging, no postTrim merge-back). Resolve two documented contradictions with the deprecated sibling — the circle parameter domain (0..1 vs 0..2π and where t=0 sits) and the closed-curve segment count (N vs N+1) — and pin down how the structured API signals errors/no-ops (VOID vs structured-empty vs error code). Finally, audit the guide's weaker claims (undoability, construction-line/rigidSet trimmability carried over from the trim workflow) and flag any doc discrepancies for correction.
methodsToCover: sketch.getPositions (line/arc segment endpoints — the spatial proof)
sketch.getPoints (circle centerId, line start/end point ids)
part.create + sketch.create (planeId setup via work-geometry tree)
questions: Does splitCurve return exactly Array<{sourceId, splittedCurves:[{id, interval}]}> with no extra leaked keys (e.g. partOf), interval being a 2-element number array?
Is result.length === splits.length, with result[i].sourceId === splits[i].geomId, order-preserving?
On an OPEN curve, do N split values produce exactly N+1 segments?
Are values normalized [0,1] fractions that map LINEARLY along the curve (0.25 on a 0..100 line lands at world x=25; 0.4 on a skew line lands at the chord lerp)?
Are intervals true contiguous [0,1] fractions: first t0=0, last t1=1, each segment's t1 == next t0, widths sum to 1, and do they cross-check against measured segment endpoint coordinates?
Is the original geomId replaced/invalidated after the split (absent from getGeometry, getPositions on it errors), or does it survive?
Are the returned segment ids new, distinct, real, and queryable via getPositions?
CIRCLE: where is t=0 (the seam) — is it +X/CCW or kernel-assigned? Discover it numerically, do not assume.
CIRCLE: how many segments does ONE value yield on a closed curve (1 reopened vs 2 vs error)? Does N+1 break for closed curves (expect N)?
CIRCLE: are values [0,1] fractions (new doc) or 0..2π (deprecated doc)? Resolve via angle math on the cut vertex.
How are intervals encoded for the wrap-around segment of a circle (e.g. [0.75,1.25] vs [0.75,0.25] vs split [0,0.25]+[0.75,1])?
How does splitCurve signal failure: VOID (splitCurves style), structured-empty entry, or error code (>=51)? Does result.length stay == splits.length on a bad geomId?
What happens at boundary values [0], [1], [0,1] — no-op, degenerate zero-length segment, or error?
What happens with duplicate values [0.5,0.5], near-duplicates within epsilon, and unsorted values [0.75,0.25] — dedup, degenerate segment, internal sort, or input-order intervals?
What happens with out-of-range values [-0.2], [1.5], and mixed valid+invalid [0.5,1.5] — clamp, extrapolate, error, drop-bad, or atomic-fail?

What error codes do missing id / missing splits / missing geomId / missing values produce (expect 1004/1006 family)? What about wrong-type id (part id, sketch-as-geomId, point-as-geomId, foreign-sketch curve)?
Is splitCurve standalone — does it stage into SplittedCurves/NoneSplitted containers like preTrim (NO expected), and is postTrim after a bare splitCurve a no-op or error?
Does splitCurve split construction lines and rigidSet members (which the trim workflow refuses), and does it auto-wire the cut point with an Auto_Coinc coincidence constraint?
Do constraints/dimensions on the original curve survive the split (in place, recreated with new ids, or dropped), and is the post-split sketch still solver-live (updateDimension returns 1)?
Is there any general undo API (common.undo / sketch.undo)? If not, is the real reverse a merge-back (postTrim/splitCurvesMergeBack), and is the guide's 'standard undo mechanism' claim unbacked?
Is splitCurve solver-dependent — does it work identically on a planeless (dead-solver) sketch?
setupNotes: Every script is `export default async function (api, { snapshot, filewrite }) { ... }`. Standard setup: `const partR = await api.v1.part.create({ name: 'SplitCurve' }); const partId = partR.result;` then find the Top work plane from the structure tree (DO NOT hardcode 38 — IDs drift): `const topPlane = Object.values(partR.structure.tree).find(n => n.class === 'CC_WorkPlane' && n.name === 'Top'); const skId = (await api.v1.sketch.create({ id: partId, planeId: topPlane.id })).result`. All coordinates MUST have Z=0 (non-zero Z = hard error 1014). The canonical probe curve is a horizontal line from [0,0,0] to [100,0,0] so world-x == 100*parameter — turning every [0,1] claim into a one-number arithmetic check. getPositions WORKS on line and arc ids (returns {startPos,endPos}); getPositions FAILS on circle ids — for circles use getPoints->centerId->getPositions for the center, and read the resulting ARC segment ids directly with getPositions for cut points. After a split, the original geomId is expected to be invalid — always read the returned splittedCurves[].id, never the original. Shared reusable per-script logging helper: log `maxLevel`, `messages.length`, `result` type/length one-liners with console.log, and `filewrite(r.result, 'NN-result')` the full structured array (small) for every script as primary evidence. Snapshots are corroboration only (a split line looks identical to an unsplit line) — never the proof of WHERE a cut landed. maxLevel buckets: <=31 success, 41-50 warning, >=51 error. Tolerance for coordinate equality: 1e-6 (solver is exact to ~15 sig figs, so a wrong-parameter bug would be off by tens of mm, not 1e-6).

scripts.title: Happy path: split a line at 0.5, verify full result shape
scripts.question: Does splitCurve on a line at values:[0.5] succeed and return exactly Array<{sourceId, splittedCurves:[{id, interval}]}> with the documented shape and no leaked keys?
scripts.setup: Line [0,0,0]->[100,0,0] on a Top-plane sketch.
scripts.call: api.v1.sketch.splitCurve({ id: skId, splits: [{ geomId: line, values: [0.5] }] })
scripts.expected: maxLevel<=31; result.length===1; result[0].sourceId===line; splittedCurves.length===2; Object.keys(result[0]).sort()===['sourceId','splittedCurves']; Object.keys(splittedCurves[0]).sort()===['id','interval']; interval is 2 numbers.
scripts.measurement: filewrite(r.result,'01-result'); console.log keys of result[0] and splittedCurves[0], splittedCurves.length, maxLevel. Assert no extra keys (flag partOf if present).

scripts.title: Spatial proof: 0.25 cut on 0..100 line lands at world [25,0,0]
scripts.question: Are values normalized [0,1] fractions mapping linearly, and do intervals match measured coordinates?
scripts.setup: Line [0,0,0]->[100,0,0]; record pre-split getPositions to lock param origin (start=param0).
scripts.call: api.v1.sketch.splitCurve({ id: skId, splits: [{ geomId: line, values: [0.25] }] })
scripts.expected: intervals [0,0.25] and [0.25,1]; cut vertex at [25,0,0].
scripts.measurement: getPositions on both segment ids. Assert segA.endPos≈[25,0,0], segB.startPos≈[25,0,0] (shared vertex, ε=1e-6), and segA.startPos≈[0,0,0], segB.endPos≈[100,0,0]. Cross-check three ways: ==[25,0,0] analytic, ==lerp(pre.start,pre.end,0.25), and interval.t1*100==25. filewrite both positions.

scripts.title: N values -> N+1 segments with contiguous intervals (line)
scripts.question: Do 2 values produce 3 segments with contiguous intervals [0,0.25],[0.25,0.75],[0.75,1] that cover [0,1], cross-checked spatially?
scripts.call: api.v1.sketch.splitCurve({ id: skId, splits: [{ geomId: line, values: [0.25,0.75] }] })
scripts.expected: 3 segments; intervals exactly [0,0.25],[0.25,0.75],[0.75,1]; cut chain world [0]->[25]->[75]->[100].
scripts.measurement: Assert splittedCurves.length===3; each interval; t0 of first==0, t1 of last==1, each seg.t1==next.t0, widths sum to 1. getPositions on all 3: shared vertices [25,0,0] and [75,0,0]. The middle segment (both ends interior) is the strongest check. filewrite result + positions.

scripts.title: Skew non-unit line: 0.4 cut proves true 2D lerp and param-0 end
scripts.question: On a non-axis-aligned, non-unit line, does 0.4 land at the chord lerp (proving linear 2D normalization and that param0==startPos)?
scripts.call: api.v1.sketch.splitCurve({ id: skId, splits: [{ geomId: line, values: [0.4] }] })
scripts.expected: intervals [0,0.4],[0.4,1]; cut vertex at [22,36,0] (= A+0.4*(B-A)); segA length≈20.
scripts.measurement: getPositions both segments; assert shared vertex≈[22,36,0] (if it came out [28,44,0], param0==endPos — record that finding). Compute dist(segA.start,segA.end)≈20 (=0.4*50) to tie interval width to measured length. filewrite.

scripts.title: Multi-curve call: result length and order track splits input
scripts.question: Is result.length===splits.length with result[i].sourceId===splits[i].geomId, order-preserving (not internal-id order)?
scripts.call: api.v1.sketch.splitCurve({ id: skId, splits: [{geomId:L1,values:[0.5]},{geomId:L2,values:[0.25,0.75]}] })
scripts.expected: result.length===2; result[0].sourceId===L1 (2 segs); result[1].sourceId===L2 (3 segs).
scripts.measurement: Assert sourceId index-for-index match and segment counts. Then run a second call with order swapped to confirm order tracks input, not id order. filewrite both results.

scripts.title: Original curve id is replaced/invalidated after split
scripts.question: After the split, is the original geomId absent from getGeometry and invalid for getPositions, and are segment ids new/distinct/present?
scripts.setup: Line [0,0,0]->[100,0,0]; getGeometry before to record line-id set.
scripts.call: api.v1.sketch.splitCurve({ id: skId, splits: [{ geomId: line, values: [0.5] }] })
scripts.expected: Original id absent from post getGeometry.lines; both segment ids present and distinct from original; getPositions(originalId) errors/stale.
scripts.measurement: getGeometry before/after: assert original id not in after.lines, net lines count +1, segment ids present. getPositions on original id -> capture maxLevel/messages (expect error 1006 or invalid). Assert no segment id equals original id. filewrite before/after id sets.

scripts.title: Empty values:[] — single [0,1] no-op or error?
scripts.question: Does values:[] return one segment interval [0,1] (preTrim-style) or VOID/error (splitCurves-style)?
scripts.call: api.v1.sketch.splitCurve({ id: skId, splits: [{ geomId: line, values: [] }] })
scripts.expected: Either one entry splittedCurves:[{interval:[0,1]}] (no-op) or maxLevel>=51 error. Disambiguates sibling lineage.
scripts.measurement: console.log maxLevel, splittedCurves.length. getGeometry count unchanged if no-op. filewrite result. Note which sibling style it matches.

scripts.title: Empty splits:[] — clean empty no-op
scripts.question: Does splits:[] return result:[] with maxLevel<=31 and geometry unchanged?
scripts.setup: Line present but not referenced.
scripts.call: api.v1.sketch.splitCurve({ id: skId, splits: [] })
scripts.expected: result.length===0; maxLevel<=31; getGeometry count unchanged.
scripts.measurement: Assert result.length===0, maxLevel bucket. getGeometry before/after equal. filewrite result.

scripts.title: Boundary values [0], [1], [0,1] — no-op vs degenerate zero-length
scripts.question: Does splitting AT an endpoint produce a zero-length segment (interval [0,0]/[1,1]), a clean no-op, or an error?
scripts.setup: Three fresh lines [0,0,0]->[100,0,0], one each for values:[0], values:[1], values:[0,1].
scripts.call: api.v1.sketch.splitCurve({ id: skId, splits: [{ geomId: line, values: [0] }] }) (and [1], and [0,1])
scripts.expected: Hypotheses: no-op single [0,1]; OR degenerate zero-length segment whose start==end. Symmetric for [0] and [1].
scripts.measurement: Per case: splittedCurves.length and intervals. If a [t,t] interval appears, getPositions and assert start==end (flag degenerate). Compare [0] vs [1] for endpoint asymmetry. filewrite all three.

scripts.title: Duplicate [0.5,0.5] and near-duplicate [0.5,0.5+1e-10]
scripts.question: Does a duplicate value dedup (2 segs) or create a zero-length middle segment (3 segs, interval [0.5,0.5])? Does a sub-epsilon pair create a sliver?
scripts.call: api.v1.sketch.splitCurve({ id: skId, splits: [{ geomId: line, values: [0.5,0.5] }] }) (and near-dup)
scripts.expected: Either dedup to 2 segments or a degenerate/sliver middle segment with width≈0.
scripts.measurement: splittedCurves.length; find any interval width<1e-6; if present getPositions and assert coincident endpoints (degenerate finding). filewrite both.

scripts.title: Unsorted values [0.75,0.25] — internal sort or input order?
scripts.question: Does splitCurve sort values ascending and return intervals [0,0.25],[0.25,0.75],[0.75,1], or follow input order / produce inverted intervals?
scripts.call: api.v1.sketch.splitCurve({ id: skId, splits: [{ geomId: line, values: [0.75,0.25] }] })
scripts.expected: Hypothesis: sorted ascending intervals; segments cover [0,1] contiguously.
scripts.measurement: Read returned interval order; assert ascending and contiguous. getPositions to confirm cut coords map to value (25 and 75) not array position. filewrite.

scripts.title: Out-of-range [-0.2], [1.5], and mixed [0.5,1.5] — clamp/extrapolate/error/atomic
scripts.question: How are out-of-range values handled: clamp, extrapolate beyond the curve, error, drop-bad, or atomic-fail of the whole call?
scripts.call: api.v1.sketch.splitCurve({ id: skId, splits: [{ geomId: line, values: [1.5] }] }) (and [-0.2], and [0.5,1.5])
scripts.expected: Distinguish: clamp(->[0,0,0]/[100,0,0]), extrapolate(->[-20,0,0]/[150,0,0] = serious finding), error>=51, or drop-bad. Mixed case tests per-curve atomicity.
scripts.measurement: Per case: maxLevel/messages; if segments produced, getPositions the new vertex and check sign/magnitude (extrapolation = vertex outside [0,100]). Mixed: segment count 2 (0.5 honored, 1.5 dropped) vs error vs 3. filewrite all three.

scripts.title: Missing id / splits / geomId / values — required-param enforcement
scripts.question: What error codes do missing required params produce (expect 1004 'must be provided' / 1006 family)?
scripts.setup: Line present; build 4 malformed calls.
scripts.call: splitCurve omitting id; omitting splits; splits:[{geomId:line}] (no values); splits:[{values:[0.5]}] (no geomId)
scripts.expected: 1004-class for missing id/splits/values; 1004/1006 for missing geomId.
scripts.measurement: Per call: maxLevel>=51 and message code. filewrite each {maxLevel, messages}.

scripts.title: Bad/wrong-class geomId: bogus, part id, sketch id, point id, foreign-sketch curve
scripts.question: How does the structured API signal an unsplittable/missing/wrong-class curve — error code, VOID, or structured-empty? Does result.length stay == splits.length?
scripts.setup: Get a point id via getPoints(line).startId; create a second sketch with its own line for the foreign-curve case; capture part id, sketch id.
scripts.call: splitCurve with geomId = 999999 (bogus); = partId; = skId (sketch); = a point id; = a curve id from another sketch
scripts.expected: Expect 1006 'invalid id' or class error for wrong types; KEY: does it drop the entry (result shorter than splits, contradicting 'same length') or error the whole call?
scripts.measurement: Per case: maxLevel/messages; compare result.length to splits.length; if equal, inspect that entry's splittedCurves (empty?). filewrite each. Flag any result.length!==splits.length as a doc discrepancy.

scripts.title: Circle, single value [0.25]: closed-curve segment count + discover t=0 seam
scripts.question: How many segments does ONE value yield on a closed circle (1 reopened vs 2 vs error), and WHERE is t=0 (discover numerically, do not assume +X)?
scripts.setup: Circle centerPos [0,0,0] radius 50. getPoints->centerId->getPositions to confirm center [0,0,0] before.
scripts.call: api.v1.sketch.splitCurve({ id: skId, splits: [{ geomId: circle, values: [0.25] }] })
scripts.expected: Likely 1 arc (reopened loop) OR 2 arcs OR error — N+1 expected to BREAK for closed curve. Cut point on radius 50.
scripts.measurement: splittedCurves.length + maxLevel. getGeometry: did circle become arc(s)? getPositions on resulting arc seg(s): read start/end, assert hypot(x,y)≈50, compute atan2 angle. The measured first-arc start angle REVEALS the seam — report the actual angle, do not force +X. getPoints->centerId->getPositions: center still [0,0,0]. filewrite.

scripts.title: Circle [0.25,0.75]: 2 arcs, [0,1]-vs-2pi domain, wrap-interval encoding
scripts.question: Do 2 values give 2 arcs at the expected angles (resolving 0..1 vs 0..2pi), and how is the wrap-around interval encoded?
scripts.setup: Circle center [0,0,0] r50; use the seam discovered in script 15 to predict cut points; values:[0.25,0.75].
scripts.call: api.v1.sketch.splitCurve({ id: skId, splits: [{ geomId: circle, values: [0.25,0.75] }] })
scripts.expected: 2 arcs; if [0,1] angular from discovered seam, cuts are 0.25 and 0.75 of the turn apart (e.g. [0,50,0] and [0,-50,0] if seam at +X CCW). Resolves circle domain.
scripts.measurement: splittedCurves.length===2; getPositions both arcs: shared cut points coincide between arcs; compute angles, assert == value*360deg from discovered seam (proves [0,1] not 2pi-literal). Record verbatim how the wrap interval is encoded ([0.75,1.25] vs [0.75,0.25] vs [0,0.25]+[0.75,1]). filewrite.

scripts.title: Open arc split: N+1 holds and arc t=0 is unambiguous
scripts.question: On an open quarter arc, does values:[0.5] give 2 sub-arcs with the cut at the angular midpoint (45deg), confirming N+1 holds for open non-linear curves?
scripts.setup: arcByCenter startPos [50,0,0], endPos [0,50,0], centerPos [0,0,0], isClockwise false (90deg CCW quarter, r50); values:[0.5].
scripts.call: api.v1.sketch.splitCurve({ id: skId, splits: [{ geomId: arc, values: [0.5] }] })
scripts.measurement: getPositions both sub-arcs (arcs ARE queryable): shared cut vertex≈[35.355,35.355,0], hypot≈50. Confirms arc param fraction from its own start (open => t=0 unambiguous, unlike circle). filewrite + intervals.

scripts.title: Standalone: no SplittedCurves/NoneSplitted staging; postTrim after split is no-op/error
scripts.question: Does splitCurve commit immediately without staging containers (unlike preTrim), and is postTrim after a bare splitCurve a harmless no-op or an error?
scripts.call: api.v1.sketch.splitCurve({ id: skId, splits: [{ geomId: line, values: [0.5] }] }) then api.v1.sketch.postTrim({ id: skId })
scripts.expected: Post-split structure tree has NO SplittedCurves/NoneSplitted containers (standalone confirmed); segments immediately live in getGeometry; postTrim is no-op (maxLevel<=31) or error — record which.
scripts.measurement: After split, scan r.structure / getGeometry for SplittedCurves|NoneSplitted (assert absent). getPositions on a segment works immediately (no finalize). Then postTrim and log maxLevel/messages. As contrast, in same script run preTrim on a separate intersecting pair and assert the containers DO appear. filewrite both structures.

scripts.title: Contrast vs deprecated splitCurves (flat array)
scripts.question: On identical geometry, does splitCurve return structured [{sourceId,splittedCurves:[{id,interval}]}] while splitCurves returns flat Array<Array<id>> with no sourceId/interval?
scripts.setup: Two identical lines L1,L2 [0,0,0]->[100,0,0]; same values [0.25,0.75].
scripts.call: api.v1.sketch.splitCurve({id:skId,splits:[{geomId:L1,values:[0.25,0.75]}]}) and api.v1.sketch.splitCurves({id:skId,splits:[{geomId:L2,values:[0.25,0.75]}]})
scripts.expected: splitCurve: structured, intervals [0,0.25],[0.25,0.75],[0.75,1]. splitCurves: flat [[id,id,id]] (N+1 ids), no sourceId/interval. Both 3 segments.
scripts.measurement: filewrite both raw results side by side. Assert splitCurve[0] has keys sourceId+splittedCurves; splitCurves[0] is a plain id array. getPositions a segment from each to confirm both cut at world x=25/75 (same underlying split). This is the teaching artifact for the rename.

scripts.title: Does splitCurve split construction lines / rigidSet members (trim refuses)?
scripts.question: Does splitCurve split a construction line and a rigidSet member — geometry the trim workflow refuses — and does it leave a dangling rigidSet reference?
scripts.setup: Case A: line with isConstruction:true. Case B: two lines + rigidSet({geomIds:[l1,l2]}), then split l1.
scripts.call: api.v1.sketch.splitCurve({ id: skId, splits: [{ geomId: constructionLine, values: [0.5] }] }) ; and on a rigidSet member
scripts.expected: Hypothesis (likely surprising): splitCurve DOES split both (different op than trim) — contradicting the guide's blanket trimmability claim. Else single [0,1] no-op.
scripts.measurement: splittedCurves.length>1 and getPositions cut coord proves a real split. For rigidSet: filewrite the rigidSet structure node and check whether it still references the now-replaced curve id (dangling = HIGH finding). filewrite both.

scripts.title: Constraint/dimension fate across a split + solver still live
scripts.question: Do constraints/dimensions on the original curve survive the split (in place / recreated new-id / dropped), and is the sketch still solver-live afterward?
scripts.setup: Line [0,0,0]->[100,0,0] with a FIXATION on the start point + a length/distance dimension. Record getGlobalState counts and getObjectInfo(line).constraints[]/.dimensions[] BEFORE.
scripts.call: api.v1.sketch.splitCurve({ id: skId, splits: [{ geomId: line, values: [0.5] }] })
scripts.expected: Determine: counts change? which segment inherits the fixation? dimension migrates/survives/drops? Contrast with postTrim's 'recreated with new ids' rule.
scripts.measurement: getGlobalState constraintCount/dimensionCount before/after. getObjectInfo on each new segment for constraints/dimensions. Then updateDimension on a surviving dimension -> assert result:1 (solver live). filewrite before/after object info.

scripts.title: Undo claim probe: no general undo API; merge-back as real reverse
scripts.question: Is there a general undo (common.undo / sketch.undo)? If not, can postTrim/splitCurvesMergeBack merge split segments back, and is the guide's 'standard undo mechanism' claim unbacked?
scripts.setup: Line [0,0,0]->[100,0,0]; getGeometry ids before; split at 0.5.
scripts.call: Probe api.v1.common.undo({}) and api.v1.sketch.undo({}) (expect unknown-method error); then api.v1.sketch.postTrim({id:skId}) / splitCurvesMergeBack after a bare split
scripts.expected: common.undo / sketch.undo do not exist -> error IS the finding. postTrim/mergeBack either restores one curve (the real reverse) or no-ops. Mark undo UNVERIFIED if no endpoint reachable (do not assert).
scripts.measurement: Capture maxLevel/messages for each undo probe (expect unknown method). After mergeBack, getGeometry: is the original single curve restored (segment count back to 1)? filewrite all probe results. Explicitly flag guide line 46 'standard undo mechanism' as unbacked if no undo API exists.

scripts.title: Solver independence: split on a planeless (dead-solver) sketch
scripts.question: Does splitCurve work identically on a planeless sketch (dead solver), proving it is a topological/geometry op independent of the constraint solver?
scripts.setup: Sketch created WITHOUT planeId (dead solver); line [0,0,0]->[100,0,0]; split at 0.5. Compare head-to-head with the same split on a planeId sketch.
scripts.call: api.v1.sketch.splitCurve({ id: planelessSkId, splits: [{ geomId: line, values: [0.5] }] })
scripts.expected: Hypothesis: splits identically (cut at [50,0,0]) -> solver-independent. If it silently no-ops (like dimensions do planeless), that mirrors the dimension trap.
scripts.measurement: splittedCurves.length===2; getPositions cut vertex≈[50,0,0] identical to the planeId twin. Compare maxLevel. filewrite both.

spatialClaims.claim: On a 0..100 line, value 0.25 places the cut vertex at world [25,0,0] (values are linear normalized fractions, param0==startPos).
spatialClaims.howToProve: getPositions on both returned segment ids; assert the shared vertex segA.endPos==segB.startPos≈[25,0,0] within 1e-6, cross-checked against lerp(start,end,0.25) and interval.t1*100==25 (script 02).

spatialClaims.claim: N values produce N+1 segments on an OPEN curve with contiguous intervals covering exactly [0,1].
spatialClaims.howToProve: values:[0.25,0.75] -> assert splittedCurves.length===3, intervals [0,0.25],[0.25,0.75],[0.75,1], each seg.t1==next.t0, widths sum to 1, and shared world vertices [25,0,0] and [75,0,0] via getPositions (script 03).

spatialClaims.claim: Normalization is a true 2D chord lerp, not axis-aligned coincidence; param0 is the startPos end.
spatialClaims.howToProve: skew line [10,20,0]->[40,60,0] at 0.4 -> assert cut vertex≈[22,36,0] (=A+0.4*(B-A)) and segA measured length≈20 (=0.4*50); a [28,44,0] result would prove param0==endPos (script 04).

spatialClaims.claim: The original curve id is replaced/invalidated; segment ids are new, distinct, and queryable.
spatialClaims.howToProve: getGeometry before/after: original id absent from after.lines, count +1; getPositions(originalId) errors; no segment id equals original; getPositions on each segment returns valid endpoints (scripts 02,06).

spatialClaims.claim: A closed circle does NOT follow N+1: one value yields 1 (or 2) arc(s), not 2; and t=0 (seam) is at a specific, measurable angle (NOT assumed +X).
spatialClaims.howToProve: split circle r50 at [0.25]; read resulting arc segment endpoints via getPositions (arcs are queryable), assert hypot≈50, compute atan2 of the first arc start to REVEAL the seam empirically; count segments to test N-vs-N+1 (scripts 15,16).

spatialClaims.claim: Circle values are [0,1] angular fractions (resolving the deprecated 0..2pi note): 0.25 == quarter turn from the seam.
